Outbound redirect handler (src/app/go/[slug]/route.ts). The visitor flow is a 302: a registered slug redirects to the vendor's external site (unreachable from the isolated verification browser), an unregistered slug to this origin's /tools. That hop is consumed by the browser navigation and stays unobservable to the recorder (re-checked 2026-10-14: an expectResponse for GET /go/zzz-verify-test reports no response within 8s and the record only carries the landed document), so the handler exposes the same resolution as a same-origin JSON read — `?format=json` returns { slug, registered, destination } with 200 and no redirect, which is the declared request. The redirect's same-origin landing (a marked GET of /tools after loading a slug with no destination) is verified alongside it.

decisions.reason: The 「◯◯を見る」 button opens /go/<slug>, whose handler 302-redirects the reader to the vendor's own page — an external service the isolated verification browser cannot reach, so the external destination itself stays locally unprovable. The handler's same-origin behavior is declared as the `outboundGo` operation (unregistered slug /go/zzz-verify-test → 302 → this origin's /tools). The handler stores no data.
evidence: src/app/go/[slug]/route.ts — NextResponse.redirect(target.url, 302) to the destination in src/lib/affiliates.ts; a slug with no destination redirects to /tools on the same origin

The verification browser is network-isolated: /go/zapier aborts with ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED, and /go/zzz-verify-test consumes its 302 during the initial navigation, so debug_page never observes the response (screenshots/debug-desktop-go_zzz-verify-test-1791637268260.json)
